topics.title: Going to (Future Plans)
topics.explanation: We use "am/is/are + going to + verb" to talk about plans and intentions for the future.
topics.explanationAr: نستخدم "am/is/are + going to + الفعل" للحديث عن خطط ونوايا للمستقبل.

examples.en: I am going to visit my grandma.
She is going to study tonight.
We are going to travel this summer.
Are you going to come to the party?

topics.title: Will (Future Predictions)
topics.explanation: We use "will + base verb" to make predictions or promises about the future, often without a fixed plan.
topics.explanationAr: نستخدم "will + الفعل الأساسي" لتوقع أو الوعد بشيء في المستقبل، غالبا دون خطة ثابتة.

examples.en: It will rain tomorrow.
I will help you.
She will be a great doctor.
They won't be late.

topics.title: Present Continuous for Future Plans
topics.explanation: We can also use the Present Continuous to talk about fixed, arranged plans in the near future.
topics.explanationAr: يمكننا أيضا استخدام المضارع المستمر للحديث عن خطط مؤكدة ومرتبة في المستقبل القريب.

examples.en: I am meeting my friend tomorrow.
We are having a party on Saturday.
She is starting a new class next week.
Are you coming to school tomorrow?

topics.title: Past Continuous (full)
topics.explanation: Past Continuous often appears with Past Simple to show one action interrupting another that was already in progress.
topics.explanationAr: غالبا ما يظهر الماضي المستمر مع الماضي البسيط ليوضح فعلا قاطع فعلا آخر كان مستمرا بالفعل.

examples.en: I was watching TV when you called.
She was sleeping when the phone rang.
While we were walking, it started to rain.
What were you doing at 7pm yesterday?
examples.ar: ماذا كنت تفعل الساعة السابعة مساء بالأمس؟

topics.title: Have to / Don't have to
topics.explanation: "Have to" shows something is necessary. "Don't have to" shows something is not necessary (but still okay to do).
topics.explanationAr: "Have to" توضح أن شيئا ضروري. "Don't have to" توضح أن شيئا غير ضروري (لكن لا بأس بفعله).

examples.en: I have to finish my homework.
You don't have to come if you're tired.
examples.ar: لا يجب أن تأتي إذا كنت متعبا.

examples.en: She has to wake up early.
We don't have to wear a uniform today.
examples.ar: لا يجب أن نرتدي الزي اليوم.

topics.title: Adverbs of Manner
topics.explanation: Adverbs of manner (usually adjective + -ly) describe how an action is done.
topics.explanationAr: ظروف الطريقة (عادة صفة + -ly) تصف كيف يتم فعل ما.

examples.en: She sings beautifully.
He runs quickly.
They worked carefully.
Please speak quietly.

topics.title: Comparatives & Superlatives with Long Adjectives
topics.explanation: For longer adjectives (usually 2+ syllables), we use "more" for comparatives and "the most" for superlatives, instead of -er/-est.
topics.explanationAr: للصفات الأطول (عادة مقطعان أو أكثر)، نستخدم "more" للمقارنة و"the most" للتفضيل، بدلا من -er/-est.

examples.en: This book is more interesting than that one.
examples.ar: هذا الكتاب أكثر إثارة للاهتمام من ذاك.

examples.en: She is the most beautiful singer.
Math is more difficult than art.
This is the most expensive toy.
